To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have successfully extended the applicability of the autoregressive model of dynamic textures to capture more complex motion patterns by including higher-order dynamics, and have shown that Burg’s spectral estimation technique can be used to reliably and efficiently estimate the parameters of such higher-order autoregressive models, even with small amounts of training data.
the use of higher order AR processes in the modeling of dynamic textures is a promising approach to improve the quality of the results.

We extend the autoregressive model for dynamic textures to include more temporal information in the model, and we show that it is possible to estimate the model parameters using a smaller amount of training data than previously reported, while maintaining the perceptual quality of the results.

the following questions: How do we model the motion in dynamic textures?
the development of models for the generation of dynamic textures.
the development of higher-order autoregressive models for the synthesis and analysis of dynamic textures.

our approach provides a very good approximation to natural dynamic texture sequences.
the proposed method is a significant contribution to the field of dynamic texture synthesis.
the higher-order autoregressive model is the best model to capture complex motion, while the first-order autoregressive is the best model for capturing simple motion.

we have developed a new method to capture and synthesize dynamic texture, which can be used for applications such as video coding, video synthesis, and image compression.
our models are able to capture more complex dynamics than earlier models, and are more robust in terms of model stability.
we are able to synthesize dynamic textures which exhibit more complex motion patterns than previously possible.

by including more temporal information, the model can capture the complex motion of dynamic textures.
the inclusion of higher order dynamics in the model allows the synthesis of perceptually accurate results with fewer frames of training data.
the higher the temporal order of the AR-model, the more complex the motion pattern that can be captured, and the more realistic the synthesized sequences become.
